name: io.github.benniledl/mail2mail
title: mail2mail.link
description: Copies all e-mail from one mailbox to another over IMAP, JMAP or POP3. Free, no account needed.

tools.name: find_mail_server
tools.description: Looks up the mail server of an e-mail address and tells what the user must do before mail2mail can log in (for example: Gmail and iCloud need an app password, GMX and WEB.DE need IMAP switched on). Optional: start_move looks the servers up by itself. Use it to prepare the user before asking for passwords.

tools.name: start_move
tools.description: Copies all e-mail (every folder) from old mailboxes to new ones: one mailbox, or up to 50 in one move (mailboxes), e.g. a whole team or company. Nothing is deleted or changed in the old mailboxes; messages already in a new mailbox are not copied twice. mail2mail first logs in to every mailbox and counts the messages, then copies by itself (several mailboxes at the same time) and checks that every message arrived. Afterwards it keeps copying new mail for follow_days (default 7), because mail still reaches the old mailbox until the switch of the address (MX records) has spread; this only adds messages to the new mailbox and never changes or deletes anything there. The passwords are stored encrypted so that only the move's token (its private link) can unlock them, for resync_move; they are deleted with the move (forget_move, or 30 days after its last activity). While the copy, the follow-up or a resync_move runs, the server can read the mail and use the passwords. So recommend app passwords where the provider offers them: they can be revoked at any time. Before calling, show the user the terms (https://mail2mail.link/terms) and the privacy notice (https://mail2mail.link/privacy), and get their OK. Set accept_terms only after they agree. Use app passwords where the provider needs them (Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo; find_mail_server says so). Microsoft 365 / Outlook.com mailboxes can't use a password: leave that password empty and give the user the returned progress_url so they can click “Sign in with Microsoft”. Several mailboxes: put them in one move (mailboxes) rather than one move each; one token, one progress page, and the mailboxes copy in parallel. You may also call start_move several times (separate moves, e.g. different options); they run at the same time. Give the user progress_url, their private page to watch or stop the move, or for several moves the moves_url that move_status returns for all their tokens (one page with every move). Then follow them with move_status (wait_seconds lets it wait for the next change instead of polling). Also pass on the returned notice about statistics. When the address stays the same and only the provider changes (or both addresses have the same domain), set new_server to the new provider's IMAP server (ask the user; it is in the new provider's setup instructions): looking it up from the address finds the old provider, and such a move is refused. The service is free; please don't abuse it.

accept_terms.description: true only after the user has seen and accepted the terms and the privacy notice.

exclude.description: Optional folder names (or patterns with *) not to copy, e.g. ["Spam", "Trash"].

follow_days.description: Optional: after the copy, keep copying new mail from the old mailbox for this many days (0 = off, default 7). Leave the default unless the user says otherwise: mail sent to the address can still arrive at the old mailbox for hours to days after the switch. If the server reboots in that time, the follow-up continues at the next call with the token (e.g. move_status). Use 0 if the user won't need the old mailbox after the copy (the passwords stay stored for resync_move until forget_move). resync_move can start it again later.

language.description: Optional: language of the pages linked in the answer (default en).

mailboxes.description: Several mailboxes in one move (up to 50), instead of the single old_/new_ fields. Each entry has the same fields; old_server / new_server above apply to entries that leave them empty. If some entries are wrong, nothing is started and the error names each one (mailboxes[i]).

new_email.description: One mailbox: address of the mailbox to copy to.

new_password.description: One mailbox: password or app password of the new mailbox (empty for Microsoft).

new_server.description: IMAP server of the new mailbox; with mailboxes, the default for entries without one. Strongly recommended, and required when both addresses have the same domain (e.g. the same address at a new provider); otherwise found automatically.

new_username.description: One mailbox: optional login name, only if it is not the e-mail address.

old_email.description: One mailbox: address of the mailbox to copy from. For several, use mailboxes instead.

old_password.description: One mailbox: password or app password of the old mailbox (empty for Microsoft).

old_server.description: Optional IMAP server name of the old mailbox (e.g. imap.example.com); with mailboxes, the default for entries without one. If empty, it is looked up from the address, which finds the server the domain points to today.

old_username.description: One mailbox: optional login name, only if it is not the e-mail address.

since.description: Optional: only copy messages received after this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: move_status
tools.description: Tells where one or several moves stand: one sentence per move for the user (summary) plus details per mailbox. Status: waiting (needs a password or Microsoft sign-in on the progress page), checking, ready, queued, running, done, attention (finished, some messages not copied), failed, stopped. moves_url is one page (Your moves) showing every given move live, with stop and continue buttons: give it to the user when there are several moves. Follow a move until done, attention, failed or stopped (finished / all_finished = true), and report the summary to the user. wait_seconds (up to 50) makes the call wait until a move reaches a new state (e.g. queued → running → done, or a mailbox fails) and then answer; use it instead of calling every 30–60 seconds. A big mailbox takes hours: you may stop following and leave the user the page. After done or attention, following = true means new mail is still being copied until follow_until (follow_added: messages added since); there is no need to keep following that. can_resync = true: resync_move can copy mail that arrived since (resyncing while it runs). can_retry = true: retry_move tries the mailboxes again that failed or did not get everything copied and checked (pairs[].retry). After a server restart, the first call with a move's token lets its interrupted work (copy, follow-up, re-sync) continue with the stored passwords.

language.description: Optional: language of the linked pages (default en).

tokens.description: Several moves at once: their tokens (instead of token, or in addition).

wait_seconds.description: Optional: wait up to this many seconds for a move to reach a new state before answering (returns at once if all are finished).

tools.name: cancel_move
tools.description: Stops a move at once, only when the user asks for it. Everything copied so far stays in the new mailbox; nothing is deleted. The passwords leave memory; their encrypted copy stays until forget_move or 30 days after the last activity, so resync_move can pick up later. After the move has finished, it stops copying new mail (status stays done). Several moves: pass tokens.

tokens.description: Several moves at once: their tokens (instead of token, or in addition).

tools.name: resync_move
tools.description: For a move that is done, attention or stopped (move_status: can_resync): copies the mail that arrived in the old mailbox since (for a stopped move: the rest of the copy, then new mail is copied for follow_days as after any move), with the stored passwords. Only adds messages to the new mailbox: nothing there is changed or deleted, messages copied before are not copied twice, and for a finished move folders the user deleted there are not filled again. Typical use: the user switched the address (MX records) after the copy or its follow-up ended. Optional follow_days keeps copying new mail afterwards for that many days. If a stored password is not accepted any more (e.g. the app password was deleted), the answer says so (needs_passwords): ask the user and call again with old_password / new_password. Then follow it with move_status (wait_seconds) until resyncing is false (for a stopped move: until status is done, attention, failed or stopped), and tell the user the summary.

follow_days.description: Optional: afterwards keep copying new mail for this many days (0 = off).

new_password.description: Only if the answer asked for it: the new mailbox's password (moves with one mailbox).

old_password.description: Only if the answer asked for it: the old mailbox's password (moves with one mailbox).

tools.name: retry_move
tools.description: For a finished move where some mailboxes failed or did not get everything copied and checked, or where new mail could not be copied (move_status: can_retry, pairs[].retry), typically because a password was refused or a server refused messages or folders for a while: checks and copies those mailboxes again (messages that were not copied are tried again), with the stored passwords or the ones given. The other mailboxes are left alone (new mail of theirs keeps being copied). Like a re-sync it only adds messages to the new mailbox. If a password is missing or was refused, the answer says so (needs_passwords): ask the user for that password (move_status: pairs[].from/to.ready is false) and call again. With one failed mailbox use old_password / new_password; with several, passwords (one entry per mailbox, in the move's order; only the retried mailboxes are read). Then follow it with move_status (wait_seconds) until status is done or attention again, and tell the user the summary.

new_password.description: Only if the answer asked for it: the failed mailbox's new password (one failed mailbox).

old_password.description: Only if the answer asked for it: the failed mailbox's old password (one failed mailbox).

passwords.description: Several failed mailboxes: passwords per mailbox in the move's order; empty strings keep the stored ones.

tools.name: forget_move
tools.description: Only when the user asks for it: stops the move and deletes what mail2mail keeps for it at once (addresses, servers, progress, the stored passwords; only the statistics line remains, and the server log for 14 days). The mail already copied stays in the new mailbox. The token stops working.
